title: One Builder Warranty per Home — Bridgewell New Home Builder Warranties Enrollment Rule
content:
## The rule

1. A home is enrolled in Bridgewell's New Home Builder Warranties once, by its builder, at its first sale.
2. A home is not enrolled when a warranty for the same property address is in status enrollment pending, workmanship period, systems period or structural period.
3. A builder warranty does not exclude a homeowner service contract on the same home: during the builder's workmanship and systems periods, defects in construction are claimed under this warranty, while ordinary wear failures of appliances and systems are handled under any homeowner service contract the owner holds.

## How clause 2 is judged

- **What is compared:** the property address of the home being enrolled against the property address of every existing New Home Builder Warranty.
- **What decides it:** the status shown on the company's warranty record, not anything the caller states.
- **When it is judged:** before the enrollment is made.

| Existing warranty at the same property address | Effect on a new enrollment of that home |
|---|---|
| None | Clause 2 does not stand in the way |
| One in status enrollment pending | Not enrolled |
| One in status workmanship period | Not enrolled |
| One in status systems period | Not enrolled |
| One in status structural period | Not enrolled |
| Only warranties in status expired or voided | Clause 2 does not stand in the way |

Clause 2 bars a new enrollment only where an existing warranty at the same address is in one of the four statuses it names; a warranty that has expired or been voided does not by itself bar one under this clause. Clause 1 still limits enrollment to the home's first sale, by its builder.

## How clause 3 divides a home's problems

| Kind of problem during the builder's workmanship and systems periods | Where it is claimed |
|---|---|
| A defect in construction | Under the New Home Builder Warranty |
| An ordinary wear failure of an appliance or a system | Under any homeowner service contract the owner holds |

**Hypothetical illustration.** A homeowner whose New Home Builder Warranty is in its systems period also holds a homeowner service contract. A leak traced to a faulty pipe joint made during construction is a defect in construction and is claimed under the builder warranty; a dishwasher that wears out in ordinary use is an ordinary wear failure and is handled under the service contract.
